- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect bearish correction.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior 30-day high.  
- If sentiment swings sharply upward after a downtrend, model should not overshoot the prior 10-day average by more than 5%.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.25 range in last 5 days), reduce forecast confidence and apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
